# How-to Recipes

Use this page when you know what you want to do, but not yet which `brdr`
objects or examples to start from.

## Before you start

Check these four things first:

1. Your thematic and reference layers use the same projected CRS.
2. CRS units are meters, because `relevant_distance` is expressed in CRS units.
3. Each thematic feature has a stable unique identifier.
4. You test on a small, representative sample before processing a full dataset.

## Choose your path

| I want to... | Start with | Then read |
|---|---|---|
| Align one small geometry and understand the result | [`DictLoader`](examples/example_readme.qmd) | [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd) |
| Align two existing GeoPandas layers | [`GeoDataFrameLoader`](examples/example_geodataframeloader_geopandas_workflow.qmd) | [Export Guide](export-guide.qmd) |
| Align GeoJSON from an API or preprocessing step | [`GeoJsonLoader`](examples/example_geojsonloader.qmd) | [Examples](examples.qmd) |
| Find useful alignment distances automatically | [`predict(...)`](examples/example_predict.qmd) | [Parameter Guide](parameter-cookbook.qmd) |
| Classify candidate results for QA or batch processing | [`evaluate(...)`](examples/example_evaluate.qmd) | [Export Guide](export-guide.qmd) |
| Process only a project area and keep the rest unchanged | [`processing_area`](examples/example_processing_area.qmd) | [Parameter Guide](parameter-cookbook.qmd) |
| Align after a CRS migration | [Lambert72 to Lambert08](examples/example_lambert72_to_lambert08.qmd) | [Parameter Guide](parameter-cookbook.qmd) |
| Work with line or network-like data | [Network processor example](examples/example_networkgeometryprocessor.qmd) | [Processor Guide](processor-selection.qmd) |
| Export results for GIS, QA, or downstream automation | `to_gdf(...)`, `to_geojson(...)`, `to_gpkg(...)` | [Export Guide](export-guide.qmd) |

## How to align two project layers

This is the most common production shape: read two layers, align thematic
geometries to reference boundaries, and export a result layer.

```python
import geopandas as gpd

from brdr.aligner import Aligner
from brdr.loader import GeoDataFrameLoader

THEMATIC_ID = "theme_id"
REFERENCE_ID = "ref_id"
CRS = "EPSG:31370"

thematic = gpd.read_file("data/thematic.gpkg").to_crs(CRS)
reference = gpd.read_file("data/reference.gpkg").to_crs(CRS)

aligner = Aligner(crs=CRS)
aligner.load_thematic_data(
    GeoDataFrameLoader(_input=thematic, id_property=THEMATIC_ID)
)
aligner.load_reference_data(
    GeoDataFrameLoader(
        _input=reference,
        id_property=REFERENCE_ID,
        is_reference=True,
    )
)

aligner_result = aligner.process(relevant_distances=[0.25, 0.5, 1.0])

aligned = aligner_result.to_gdf(
    aligner=aligner,
    profile="analysis",
    add_original_attributes=True,
)
aligned.to_file("output/aligned.gpkg", layer="aligned", driver="GPKG")
```

Use this when you already know the relevant distances you want to inspect.
If you do not know them yet, use `predict(...)` or `evaluate(...)`.

## How to discover relevant distances

Alignment quality often depends on the distance range. Start with a range that
matches the expected positional deviation in your data.

```python
relevant_distances = [0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5]

predictions = aligner.predict(relevant_distances=relevant_distances)
prediction_gdf = predictions.to_gdf(
    aligner=aligner,
    profile="analysis",
    add_original_attributes=True,
)
```

Use `predict(...)` when you want a compact list of stable candidate geometries.
Use `evaluate(...)` when you also need QA classifications and scoring metadata.

```python
evaluated = aligner.evaluate(relevant_distances=relevant_distances)
evaluated_gdf = evaluated.to_gdf(
    aligner=aligner,
    profile="analysis",
    add_metadata=True,
    add_original_attributes=True,
)
```

## How to limit alignment to one area

Use `processing_area` when only part of a geometry may change. The intersecting
part is processed, while the outside part is merged back unchanged.

```python
from shapely.geometry import box

project_area = box(100000, 200000, 101000, 201000)

scoped_result = aligner.process(
    relevant_distances=[0.5, 1.0],
    processing_area=project_area,
)
```

This is useful for project areas, incremental migration, and partial QA fixes.

## How to choose a processor

Start with the default `AlignerGeometryProcessor`. Change processor only when
your data or workflow requires it.

| Use case | Processor direction |
|---|---|
| Parcel-like polygon alignment | Default or `DieussaertGeometryProcessor` |
| Mixed geometry types or network behavior | `NetworkGeometryProcessor` |
| Lines that should follow thematic anchor points | `AnchorGeometryProcessor` |
| One-way or direction-constrained routing | Directed network or directed anchor processor |
| Shared-boundary consistency between thematic features | `TopologyProcessor` |
| Explicit vertex/edge snapping workflows | `SnapGeometryProcessor` |

See the [Processor Guide](processor-selection.qmd) before changing processor
configuration in production.

## How to inspect the result

The default output contains one result per thematic feature and relevant
distance. The most important geometry fields are:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | The aligned geometry |
| `result_diff` | Total changed area or geometry |
| `result_diff_plus` | Parts added to the original thematic geometry |
| `result_diff_min` | Parts removed from the original thematic geometry |

For GIS inspection, export `profile="analysis"` to GeoPackage or GeoJSON.
For compact automation output, use `profile="minimal"`.

```python
aligner_result.to_gpkg(
    aligner=aligner,
    path="output/alignment.gpkg",
    layer="aligned",
    profile="analysis",
    add_original_attributes=True,
)
```

## Common first-run problems

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| Nothing changes | `relevant_distance` may be too small, or reference features are not close enough |
| Too much changes | `relevant_distance` may be too large for the intended business rule |
| Results look shifted | Thematic and reference data may not be in the same CRS |
| IDs are missing or duplicated | Check the loader `id_property` |
| Network examples behave unexpectedly | Confirm whether you need a network processor, directed routing, or anchor behavior |

When in doubt, run `process(...)` over a short distance series, export
`profile="analysis"`, and inspect `result_diff_plus` and `result_diff_min` in
your GIS tool.
